sit verb

also be sitting, sit down, take a seat, be seated, take your seats, back to your seats

classical

Gell. 2.21.2: sedēbāmus ergō in puppī
Cic. Amic. 2: domī in hēmicycliō sedentem
Traupman 379

sedeō, sedēre, sēdī, sessum

verb, second conjugation

sit, be sitting

The state of sitting. Sitting down is cōnsīdō, though the imperative sedē also serves for “sit down” (Mart. 8.67.6).

Other words

  • cōnsīdō, cōnsīdere, cōnsēdī, cōnsessum — sit down, take a seat; settle

    verb, third conjugation · classical · Ov. Met. 13.930–931: in illō caespite cōnsēdī; Liv. 7.26.3: corvus repente in galeā cōnsēdit; Traupman 34: cōnsīde (cōnsīdite)

    The act of sitting down, also of a bird landing. “Sit down!” is Cōnsīde!

Examples

  • sedēbāmus ergō in puppī simul ūniversī et lūcentia sīdera cōnsīderābāmus

    so we were all sitting together on the stern, gazing at the shining starsGell. 2.21.2

  • curre, age, et inlōtōs revocā, Calliste, ministrōs; sternantur lectī: Caeciliāne, sedē

    Quick, Callistus, run and call the waiters back, unwashed as they are; have the couches spread: Caecilianus, do sit downMart. 8.67.5–6

  • ego prīmus in illō caespite cōnsēdī, dum līna madentia siccō

    I was the first to sit down on that turf, while I dried my wet linesOv. Met. 13.930–931

  • Revertite ad subsellia.

    Take your seats.Traupman 34

See also sit down!, sit up straight!, sit cross-legged, seat, chair, stand.
